decision.html.text:
Mixed paths - not only the three pure choices

A real plan can mix the choices: live in Property A for a while, then sell; or rent it for a while, then sell. Because the basis reset applies to a prompt sale, waiting longer exposes any further gain to tax - so mixed paths sit between the pure outcomes.

Mixed paths versus the pure choices (illustrative; inheritance 2045; wealth in 2076, 2026 dollars)
PathWhat happensIllustrative wealth in 2076Compared with pure sellStatus
Sell immediately (pure sell)Sell at inheritance, invest $6,152,510 in stocks$9,747,210baselinemodel result IRS Topic 409
Live in Property A, then sell after 5 yearsPay lived-in tax ~$59,950/yr for 5 years, live there, then sell with basis resetmodel output - flag A02below pure sell unless the home outruns stocksillustrative IRS Topic 409
Rent Property A, then sell after 5 yearsCollect rent ~$127,740/yr, pay rented tax ~$77,480/yr for 5 years, then sell with basis resetmodel output - flag A02below pure sell unless rent is much higherillustrative IRS Topic 409
Rent indefinitely (pure rent)Keep renting, never sell$5,582,450$4,164,760 below pure sellmodel result IRS Topic 409
Reinvestment risk beside the headline. The headline plan - sell Property A and invest the proceeds in stocks - assumes the money earns a stock-like return. If the proceeds are parked in cash or Treasury bills instead (about 3.5% a year), renting comes out ahead ($5,582,450 vs $3,554,580 in 2026 dollars by 2076). That is why the plan says do not park the money. The phased-investing path on the Black swan page tests the middle ground: 24-36 months in 3M-2Y Treasuries (~4.4%), then phased into stocks, which softens 1929/2008 crash entry risk but gives up some upside if stocks keep rising.

process.html.text:
Deadline timeline after the Transferor's death

Each clock starts at the date of death. These are legal deadlines, not recommendations - missing one can cost an exemption or add a penalty.

Within 60 days
Trustee serves notice to beneficiaries and heirs; starts the 120-day contest period
Prob. Code §16061.7
Within 150 days
File the change-in-ownership statement for Property A with the Santa Clara County Assessor
R&TC §480
Within 9 months
File Form 706 (estate tax) if above the threshold, or elect portability for a surviving spouse (6-month extension via Form 4768)
IRS Form 706 instructions
Within 1 year
Only if moving in: make Property A the principal residence and file the homeowners' exemption (BOE-266) before the exclusion claim
R&TC §63.2; BOE Pub. 800-1
Within 3 years
Only if moving in: file the parent-child exclusion claim (BOE-19-P) before any transfer to a third party
R&TC §63.2; BOE Prop 19
